title: Plastering, screeding & finishes
headline: Plaster, screed, ceilings, tiles, paint, doors and windows — what you see every day.
seoTitle: Plastering, screeding, POP, tiling and painting in Nigeria: finishing guide
seoDescription: A plain-English guide to wall plastering, floor screeds, POP and gypsum ceilings, tiling, painting, doors and windows in Nigerian homes, with tricks to watch for.
summary: Finishes are where budgets overrun. Agree the exact products and samples before work starts.
whatHappens: Plastering (rendering): cement-sand plaster, about 12–15 mm thick, on walls inside and out, kept straight with guides.
Screeding: cement-sand layer on floors to level them before tiles, often 25–50 mm.
Ceilings: POP (plaster of Paris), gypsum board or PVC/fibre-cement on a hanging frame.
Tiling: floor and wall tiles bedded in adhesive or mortar, with spacers and grout.
Painting: filler/skim (often POP screeding on walls), then primer and emulsion coats inside; weather-resistant paint outside.
Doors, windows (aluminium or uPVC), burglary proofs, sanitary fittings, light fittings and final electrical and plumbing connections.
problems: Plaster mixed weak to save cement — it cracks, sounds hollow when tapped and peels.
Floors not level so tiles crack or water ponds in bathrooms; showers without proper falls to the drain.
Tiles laid without enough adhesive (hollow spots) — tap them with a coin.
Paint watered down or fewer coats than agreed; cheap paint in a branded bucket.
Doors and windows of lower quality than the sample shown.
Endless ‘small extras’ during finishing with no written price.
questions: What plaster and screed mix are you using?
Can I approve samples of tiles, paint colour and brand, doors, windows and fittings before purchase?
How many coats of paint, and what brand and product line?
How are bathroom floors laid to fall to the drain, and is there waterproofing in the shower area?
What is the snagging (defects) process and the defects liability period after handover?
photoCheckpoints: Plastered walls with a straight edge held against them.
Screed with a level showing falls in bathrooms.
Tile boxes showing brand/batch, and the back of a tile with adhesive coverage.
Paint buckets on site with brand and product visible, and the number of coats done.
Doors, windows and fittings on delivery with labels.
Room-by-room video at completion for your snag list.
